**Problem.** Determine the cardinality of the set of all equivalence relations on ℕ such that all equivalence classes have the same cardinality.

---

## Proof

Let $\mathcal{S}$ denote the set of all equivalence relations $R$ on $\mathbb{N}$ such that every equivalence class of $R$ has the same cardinality. We show $|\mathcal{S}| = 2^{\aleph_0}$.

### Upper bound: $|\mathcal{S}| \le 2^{\aleph_0}$

Every equivalence relation on $\mathbb{N}$ is a subset of $\mathbb{N}\times\mathbb{N}$. Since $|\mathbb{N}\times\mathbb{N}| = \aleph_0$, the power set $\mathcal{P}(\mathbb{N}\times\mathbb{N})$ has cardinality $2^{\aleph_0}$. Therefore
$$\mathcal{S} \subseteq \mathcal{P}(\mathbb{N}\times\mathbb{N}) \implies |\mathcal{S}| \le 2^{\aleph_0}.$$

### Lower bound: $|\mathcal{S}| \ge 2^{\aleph_0}$

We exhibit $2^{\aleph_0}$ distinct elements of $\mathcal{S}$, each having all equivalence classes of size $2$.

**Identify $\mathbb{N}$ with $\{0,1\}\times\mathbb{N}$** via any fixed bijection. For each permutation $\sigma\colon\mathbb{N}\to\mathbb{N}$ (bijection), define a partition of $\{0,1\}\times\mathbb{N}$ into pairs:
$$\bigl\{\,\{(0,j),\,(1,\sigma(j))\} : j\in\mathbb{N}\,\bigr\}.$$
This is a partition of $\{0,1\}\times\mathbb{N}$ into $2$-element sets, hence defines an equivalence relation $R_\sigma$ in which every class has cardinality $2$. Thus $R_\sigma\in\mathcal{S}$.

**Distinctness.** Given the partition (equivalently, $R_\sigma$), we recover $\sigma$ uniquely: for each $j$, the unique element paired with $(0,j)$ is $(1,\sigma(j))$, so $\sigma(j)$ is read off directly. Hence $\sigma\ne\sigma'\implies R_\sigma\ne R_{\sigma'}$.

**Counting permutations.** The set $\operatorname{Sym}(\mathbb{N})$ of all bijections $\mathbb{N}\to\mathbb{N}$ has cardinality $2^{\aleph_0}$:
- *Upper bound:* $\operatorname{Sym}(\mathbb{N})\subseteq\mathbb{N}^{\mathbb{N}}$, and $|\mathbb{N}^{\mathbb{N}}|=\aleph_0^{\aleph_0}=2^{\aleph_0}$.
- *Lower bound:* For each subset $A\subseteq\mathbb{N}$, define the permutation $\sigma_A$ that swaps $2n$ and $2n+1$ when $n\in A$, and fixes both $2n,2n+1$ when $n\notin A$. The map $A\mapsto\sigma_A$ is injective from $\mathcal{P}(\mathbb{N})$ into $\operatorname{Sym}(\mathbb{N})$, giving $|\operatorname{Sym}(\mathbb{N})|\ge 2^{\aleph_0}$.

Therefore $|\operatorname{Sym}(\mathbb{N})|=2^{\aleph_0}$, and the map $\sigma\mapsto R_\sigma$ is injective, so
$$|\mathcal{S}|\ge 2^{\aleph_0}.$$

### Conclusion

Combining both bounds:
$$|\mathcal{S}| = 2^{\aleph_0}.$$

The cardinality of the set of all equivalence relations on $\mathbb{N}$ with all equivalence classes of the same cardinality is $\boxed{2^{\aleph_0}}$ (the cardinality of the continuum).
